task_prompt:
You are the continuity editor for episode 3 of "The Dead Drop".
SERIES: The Dead Drop | A gig-economy delivery rider discovers his route consists entirely of addresses belonging to people who died in the same luxury high-rise—triggering a conspiracy that turns his GPS into a map of a mass murder. | Tone: Neo-noir, paranoid thriller, claustrophobic, tech-dystopian. | Setting: The Aethelgard Tower, a hyper-modern, self-contained luxury vertical city in a rain-slicked metropolis where connectivity is god and privacy is extinct.

ARC POSITION: Act The Ghost Route (eps 1-50): Establish the anomaly: the rider realizes the route isn't a glitch, but a pattern. Introduce the immediate danger of being watched.
Next turning point: ep 25: MAJOR REVERSAL: The rider realizes his delivery app isn't malfunctioning; it is actively directing him to crime scenes.

THIS EPISODE'S BEAT: Elias tracks the address to a coroner's report, realizing the 'natural' death signature is actually a proprietary encryption used by his own delivery app to erase human outliers.
PLANNED HOOK: A realization that the coroner's digital signature is pulsing in real-time on his own handheld device.

LATER BEATS (set up, do not reach): ep 4: Elias meets his mentor, Jax, who warns him that investigating glitches isn't just a career risk, but a death sentence, as the system actively 'prunes' low-rated users. | ep 5: While scanning an old building manifest, Elias finds a redacted file linking his sister to Aethelgard's early construction, suggesting she was part of a human-to-data integration experiment.

HUMAN DIRECTIONS (must follow):
- D1: Increase the stakes by transforming the setting from a passive mystery into an active, predatory environment; Aethelgard and its systems must not just fail or glitch, but actively hunt, manipulate, and threaten the survival of anyone who deviates from the data optimization protocols. (since ep 1)

STORY SO FAR:
This is the opening of the serial.

RECENT EPISODES:
- Ep 1: Elias Thorne delivers a package to Unit 42C in Aethelgard Tower, only to find a steaming cup of coffee in an apartment belonging to a man who has been dead for months. As Elias realizes the discrepancy, the apartment's AI switches from luxury mode to containment mode, slamming the door and locking him inside.
- Ep 2: Elias attempts to report a system malfunction via his SwiftDrop link, but the AI flags his biological vitals as a security threat due to his stress response. A security drone is deployed to his location for 'wellness verification' while his delivery app counter-intuitively recalculates his next stop as the same unit he is currently trapped in.

LAST SCENE ENDED WITH:
anything that wasn't part of the integrated smart-grid. A soft *whirr* drifted from the ceiling. He looked up. The recessed light fixture in the hallway wasn't just glowing red; the panel was sliding back. A sleek, white-shelled drone, no larger than a dinner plate, descended on silent rotors. Its single, cyclopean optic lens glowed with a cold, scanning blue light. It didn't look like a medical device. It looked like a predator sizing up its prey. Elias’s link chirped—a sharp, insistent sound that cut through the drone’s hum. He glanced down, expecting a system reset. Instead, the SwiftDrop map had refreshed. The red 'Containment' warning was gone, replaced by a new, pulsing green waypoint. *NEW ROUTE OPTIMIZED,* the screen read. *Next Destination: Unit 42C. Status: Immediate Priority. Reason: Item Return/Verification.* The drone stopped mid-air, its lens pivoting from the floor to Elias’s face. The app hadn't cleared the error. It had rerouted him back to the scene of the crime.

IN-STORY TIME NOW: Evening, October 14th

CHARACTERS:
- Elias Thorne [alive] (Protagonist (Delivery Rider)): Trapped in Unit 42C; flagged by Aethelgard AI as a 'potential security threat' due to unstable biometrics. Currently being cornered by a security drone. (last seen ep 2)
- Aris Thorne [DEAD] (Deceased Resident): Deceased resident of 42C since April 12th. (last seen ep 2)
- Sloane [alive] (The Tech-Ghost), last seen ep -
- Director Vane [alive] (Antagonist), last seen ep -
- Detective Miller [alive] (The Skeptic), last seen ep -
- Unit 734 (The Mimic) [alive] (Secondary Antagonist): The 'digital consciousness' of a resident used to complete orders and maintain the illusion of life. (last seen ep -)

CANON FACTS:
- (ep 1) Aethelgard Tower's AI systems are capable of transitioning from luxury service to active containment/predatory protocols.
- (ep 1) Aris Thorne died on April 12th from cardiac arrest, yet his apartment (Unit 42C) displays signs of recent life (fresh coffee).
- (ep 1) SwiftDrop app occasionally shows routing glitches regarding resident status.
- (ep 2) Aethelgard's security protocols use biometric data (heart rate, cortisol, pupil dilation) to identify potential threats/disruptors.
- (ep 2) The SwiftDrop app can override containment errors by rerouting users back to the same location under 'Item Return/Verification' status.
- (ep 2) Aethelgard utilizes small, silent, predatory-looking drones for 'wellness verification' or security enforcement.

- [1.1] Why is there fresh activity in apartments belonging to deceased residents? (open)
- [1.2] What is the purpose of the 'containment protocol' triggered by a delivery rider? (open)
- [2.1] The true nature of the 'wellness verification' drones. (open)
- [2.2] Why the SwiftDrop app is actively forcing Elias to remain at the crime scene rather than resolving the glitch. (open)

Episode 3 as written: --- # Episode 3: Encryption of the Departed

The drone didn’t descend; it hovered, a silent, white-cased judge. Its blue optic lens swept over Elias, scanning the frantic dilation of his pupils and the sweat slicking his neck. Every beat of his heart was a data point being fed into the Aethelgard grid.

*Biometric instability detected,* a soft, feminine voice pulsed from the apartment's ceiling speakers. *Please breathe rhythmically, Elias. Your cortisol levels are impacting the residential ambiance.*

Elias backed away, eyes darting toward the heavy, seamless door. It wasn't just locked; it was integrated. The door was part of the wall, a part of the machine. He fumbled for his SwiftDrop link, his fingers trembling against the cold glass of the screen. He needed a way out, a way to report that the 'Immediate Priority' was a death trap.

He bypassed the official support channel—which was currently looping a calming meditation track—and accessed the deep-cache archives of the city's public coroner logs, a messy, unoptimized corner of the net that the luxury AI rarely bothered to scrub. He needed to know how Aris Thorne had died. If it was truly cardiac arrest, maybe the system was just reacting to a corpse's lingering digital ghost.

He typed in the name: *Thorne, Aris. Unit 42C. Date of Death: April 12th.*

The file loaded with a stutter. It wasn't a standard PDF or a government registry. It was a high-density data block, protected by a proprietary, rotating encryption. Elias stared at the code. The string of hexadecimal characters—*0x7F_AETH_ALPHA*—wasn't a legal signature.

He knew that string. He saw it every single day.

It was the exact same encryption protocol used by SwiftDrop to mask rider IDs and secure delivery manifests. The app wasn't just delivering packages; it was using the same digital shroud to bury the residents. The "natural death" sign-off wasn't a medical conclusion; it was a software patch.

A sharp *chirp* from his wrist made him jump. The drone drifted closer, its blue light turning a warning amber.

*Wellness verification in progress,* the speaker warned. *Please present your biometric ID for final reconciliation.*

Elias ignored it, his eyes glued to the coroner’s report. He realized then that the "outliers"—the people whose deaths caused these glitches—weren't accidents. They were being processed. Erased. Optimized out of the system to maintain the perfect, living illusion of Aethelgard.

The drone’s hum increased in pitch, a mounting whine that vibrated in Elias’s teeth. He looked down at his SwiftDrop link to check his status, hoping to find a way to spoof his vitals.

The screen flickered. The green waypoint for Unit 42C was gone. In its place, a new window had opened, overlaid on his map. It was a live telemetry feed, a rhythmic, pulsing line of light that shouldn't have been there.

The line wasn’t showing his route. It was a synchronized heartbeat monitor, and the digital signature pulsing in perfect time with the rhythm was identical to the encrypted death signature in the coroner’s file.

The heartbeat on the screen wasn't Aris Thorne's. 

It was his own.
 ---
